dossier.public_summary: The dip depth alternates strongly between odd and even events and individual transits vary more than expected, with a few very deep transits driving the detection. The star is spotted and its variability period nearly matches the dip period. Together this points to stellar variability or a blended binary, not a consistent planet transit.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ at >4 sigma, strong binary signature. Sector-level odd/even also inconsistent (sector_oe_max_sigma 5.272, 2 sectors over 3).
reasons.value: 4.242 (depth_odd 1327 ppm vs depth_even 573.4 ppm, ratio 2.3, difference 753.2 ppm)

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent; top 3 transits carry most of the signal and one is 6.6 sigma outlier. Sectors appear steady only because the outliers happen to fall in one sector.
reasons.value: 4.66e-27, chi2 146.51 dof 9, share_of_top_3 0.958 with outliers 3213, 2421, 2176 ppm

reasons.why: Dip period is near-1:1 with strong stellar variability (amplitude ~2351 ppm) and fit_b 0.182 low impact parameter. Combined with odd/even difference favors spot/eclipse systematics, not a planet.
